method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb autoregressive SMILES policy optimization
method_thesis: Pretrain an autoregressive SMILES language model on the allowed unlabeled corpus and freeze a copy as the molecular prior. During each objective session, sample complete molecules de novo token by token from a trainable agent, rank the accepted molecules by their observed oracle rewards, and update the agent only on the highest-reward fraction using the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: the squared gap between agent log-likelihood and a target formed from prior log-likelihood plus scaled reward. Excluding low-reward samples from policy updates prevents them from repeatedly pulling the agent back toward the prior, while prior likelihood still regularizes the elite updates; this concentrates the scarce feedback on sequences associated with improvement of final Top-1 without screening a finite molecular pool.

applicability_conditions: Task-local oracle scores are stationary and comparable across feedback rounds, so an earlier high score remains valid evidence for the same objective.
Earlier accepted trajectories remain tokenizable under the fixed vocabulary and have finite frozen-prior likelihoods and reward-augmented targets.

Batch quality varies enough that preserving a small set of historical high-reward trajectories adds information beyond the current top half; benefit may be limited when every new batch already dominates the buffer or the objective is saturated.

A five-trajectory replay contribution is small enough that the corpus prior and unchanged current-batch elites preserve productive novelty; transfer is weaker if repeated elite pressure collapses ancestral sampling or excludes a disconnected optimum.

The evidence for the Parent and the related replay implementations is limited to screening seed 0, and the related nodes establish replay activation rather than a reliable score benefit for this Parent.
research_intent.falsifier: The mechanism did not happen if eligible post-first-round updates contain no uniquely traceable trajectory created in an earlier round, if a replay identifier is absent from or duplicated in the optimizer set, or if the aggregate paired absolute reward-augmented target gap on the exact replayed trajectories fails to decrease after optimization.
research_intent.implementation_change: Keep preparation, ancestral proposal sampling, canonicalization and duplicate rejection, the current-batch top-half rule, reward scale, optimizer, and two optimizer steps unchanged. In each objective session, store accepted generated trajectories with canonical identity, token ids, score, and creation round in a deterministic score-sorted buffer capped at 50. Before inserting the current feedback, select up to five highest-scoring entries from earlier rounds, append them once to the current five elites, and apply the existing squared Augmented Hill-Climb target-gap loss to that combined set; insert the current accepted trajectories and trim the buffer only after the update, so every replay member is strictly historical and no current trajectory is duplicated.
research_intent.mechanism: Add one bounded, task-local reward-prioritized experience memory to the Parent's Augmented Hill-Climb update: retain the 50 highest-scoring unique accepted agent trajectories and, at each later feedback round, train on the five highest-scoring trajectories that predate the current round alongside the unchanged current-batch elite half, using each stored oracle score in the same frozen-prior reward-augmented likelihood target.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The Parent has no cross-round reward memory: every one of its 145 optimizer records uses only the five elites from the immediately observed batch of ten and then drops those scored trajectories. Node n-6174d6127af5 shows that this current-batch-only signal is fragile: only 125/145 updates increased likelihood on their selected trajectories, sitagliptin_mpo was positive on only 18/29 updates, and the two weakest final task values were 0.19882131306757464 on median_2 and 0.2590041376695029 on sitagliptin_mpo even though novel-valid sampling yield remained 0.8396073778448927. Cross-round reuse is operationally feasible in campaign evidence: n-a5a9c7e8871a reused 1,346 adaptive trajectories after their creation batch, while n-f316eae4e271 measured a 0.22487942715802353 rank advantage from reward-prioritized rather than uniform replay.

applicability_conditions: Operational activation is supported when earlier task-local scores can be reused as fixed reward targets and the associated trajectories remain tokenizable with finite prior and agent likelihoods: all 700 replay uses had traceable stored scores and finite paired before/after target gaps.

The evidence supports a deterministic 50-entry task-local buffer contributing five highest-scoring historical trajectories alongside five current elites under the inherited reward scale and two optimizer steps: every one of 140 eligible updates had exactly this composition, and no buffer exceeded capacity.

Replay target-gap reduction is supported as an aggregate effect rather than a monotone per-update guarantee. The gap decreased on 119/140 updates, while sitagliptin_mpo split evenly between 14 decreases and 14 increases despite a negative task-level mean paired change.

The evidence does not establish transfer to a larger replay fraction, a different buffer policy, a nonstationary or cross-task oracle, or settings where repeated historical pressure displaces necessary novelty; those conditions were not evaluated by this node.
Evidence is limited to screening seed 0. It confirms replay execution and the preregistered intermediate gap decrease, not a reliable score benefit relative to the Parent across independent seeds.

observable_measurements.name: historical_elite_replay_target_gap
observable_measurements.parent_value: Parent n-6174d6127af5 has 145 feedback-update records, and in every record optimizer_trajectory_ids exactly equals the five identifiers selected from that same round as elite_trajectory_ids. Parsing each identifier's creation-round prefix gives zero prior-round optimizer members, matching the registered historical_optimizer_fraction reference of 0.0. The Parent has no replay buffer and therefore no paired historical-trajectory target-gap value; its historical replay target gap is undefined rather than a numeric zero.
observable_measurements.value: Seed 0 across five task sessions produced 145 feedback updates. The first update of each task correctly had an empty buffer and no historical optimizer member. Every one of the 140 eligible updates in rounds 2 through 29 selected exactly five replay trajectories alongside the unchanged five current-batch elites, for 700 historical optimizer memberships and historical_optimizer_fraction 0.5 on every eligible update. Each record contains aligned five-element lists of replay identifiers, canonical identities, creation rounds, stored scores, and buffer ranks 1 through 5. All replay members were unique within their update, strictly older than the update, and present exactly once in the ten-member optimizer set; all 700 uses trace to an accepted identifier in the stated task-local creation update and to the same canonical identity and stored score in that Evaluation Replica's trajectory, covering 136 distinct task-qualified historical trajectories. On the identical replay token trajectories, the arithmetic mean absolute length-normalized reward-augmented target gap decreased from 0.3639145763291578 before optimization to 0.34342052096534254 after optimization, an arithmetic mean paired after-minus-before change of -0.020494055363815277. The gap decreased on 119/140 updates and increased on 21/140. Every task had a negative mean paired change: deco_hop -0.045309575008494515 (28/28 decreases), drd2_docking -0.023167937727911137 (27/28), median_2 -0.009181565837934613 (23/28), sitagliptin_mpo -0.0024599376816435603 (14/28), and zaleplon_mpo -0.022351260563092574 (27/28). Thus the preregistered decrease holds in aggregate and by task mean, though not monotonically update by update.
